correctness.rationale: The actual frozen RESULT.md stratifies the entire unit sphere into same-sign Euclidean arcs, opposite-sign l1 facets, and axis junctions. The dual norm is sqrt(p²+q²) for pq≥0, max(|p|,|q|) for pq≤0; quotient-line duality computes d(x,y) on each stratum. The arc gives d=1/[(sinθ+cosθ)max(sinθ,cosθ)]≥1/sqrt2; facets give d=1/[sqrt2 sqrt(a²+b²)]≥1/sqrt2; junction x=(1,0), y=(τ,1)/sqrt(1+τ²), τ∈[0,1], gives d=1/sqrt(1+τ²)≥1/sqrt2. At τ=1 equality is attained. Signs/boundary axes are covered by the full norming-functional segment; proof is continuum, not finite sampling.

evidence: For every real two-dimensional Banach X, let d(X)=inf_{x perpendicular_B y, ||x||=||y||=1}dist(y,Rx). Given such x,y choose f in S(X*) norming x and annihilating y, and g in S(X*) annihilating x. The one-dimensional quotient identity gives dist_X(y,Rx)=|g(y)|. Since f perpendicular_B* g (normed by x), the dual reverse distance dist_(X*)(g,Rf) also equals |g(y)| because its annihilator is y in X**. The dual construction is reversible in dimension 2, so d(X)=d(X*). The Day-James ell2-ell1 dual norm is sqrt(p²+q²) for pq>=0 and max(|p|,|q|) for pq<=0. Reflecting q to -q turns it into the displayed square-circle norm, hence the two published numerical theorems are equivalent, not independent new claims.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior square-circle constant plus d(X)=d(X*) yields this Day–James parameter with no additional problem-specific optimization.
